title: Sel Roti
steps: Soak rice, grind into a smooth batter. Mix with sugar, a little milk and cardamom to a pouring consistency. Ferment lightly if desired.
Heat oil in a deep pan. Pour the batter in a circular ring shape using a ladle or cloth cone.
Deep-fry till golden and crisp on both sides.
Serve with potato curry, achar or as a festive snack with tea.

fullIngredients.name: Rice flour or soaked rice ground
Sugar or jaggery, milk or water
Cardamom, ghee or oil for frying

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Ring-shaped sweet rice bread – essential for Dashain and Tihar.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Crisp outside, soft inside; a Nepali-Sikkimese classic.

title: Chicken Thukpa
steps: Make a clear broth by simmering chicken bones with ginger, garlic and onion.
Add noodles, chopped chicken meat and vegetables. Cook till noodles are done and flavours meld.
Season with salt, pepper and a little soy. Serve hot with chilli paste on the side.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, garlic, ginger, green chilli, carrot, cabbage
Soy sauce, salt, pepper, local spices

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Hearty Tibetan-influenced noodle soup – perfect for cold mornings.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A staple comfort food in Sikkim.

title: Vegetable Thukpa
steps: Make a clear broth by simmering vegetables with ginger, garlic and onion.
Add noodles and chopped vegetables. Cook till noodles are done and flavours meld.
Season with salt, pepper and a little soy. Serve hot with chilli paste on the side.

fullIngredients.name: Soy sauce, salt, pepper, local spices

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Vegetarian version of the classic Himalayan noodle soup.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Perfect for cold mornings and monsoon days.

title: Chicken Momo
steps: Knead a soft dough for wrappers. Rest.
Mix minced chicken with finely chopped onion, ginger, garlic, cabbage and seasoning.
Roll thin wrappers, fill, pleat and steam in a bamboo steamer or momo steamer for 10–12 minutes.
Serve hot with spicy tomato-chilli chutney.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, ginger, garlic, cabbage, salt, pepper

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Sikkim's most beloved dish – Bhutia/Tibetan style with thicker skin in some homes.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Steamed or kothey (pan-fried) versions both popular.

title: Vegetable Momo
steps: Knead a soft dough for wrappers. Rest.
Mix finely chopped vegetables with ginger, garlic and seasoning.
Roll thin wrappers, fill, pleat and steam in a bamboo steamer or momo steamer for 10–12 minutes.
Serve hot with spicy tomato-chilli chutney.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Vegetarian version of Sikkim's most beloved dish.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Steamed or kothey (pan-fried) versions both popular.

title: Phagshapa
steps: Cut pork into strips. Slice radish into similar pieces.
In a pot, combine pork, radish, dried red chillies and salt. Add a little water.
Slow-cook till the pork fat renders, radish softens and the dish becomes a rich, spicy stew (no extra oil needed).
Serve with red or white rice.

fullIngredients.name: Pork belly or fatty pork strips

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Iconic Bhutia dish – pork fat provides all the richness.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Milder than many Himalayan meat dishes but deeply flavourful.

title: Gundruk ko Jhol
steps: Soak gundruk briefly if very dry. Heat mustard oil, sauté onion, garlic and chilli.
Add tomato and turmeric, then the gundruk. Add water and simmer into a light, tangy soup.
Serve with rice as a sour, probiotic side.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Fermented mustard/radish/cauliflower leaves – a winter staple and digestive aid.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: The sour flavour is distinctive and highly valued.

title: Kinema Curry
steps: Heat oil, sauté onion, ginger, garlic and chilli. Add tomato and turmeric.
Add kinema and a little water. Simmer till the flavours blend and the curry thickens slightly.
Serve with rice or as a side.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, tomato, green chilli, ginger, garlic

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Fermented soybean product unique to the eastern Himalayas – strong, umami flavour.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: An acquired taste but highly nutritious.

title: Sha Phaley
steps: Knead a soft dough. Prepare a spiced minced meat and cabbage filling.
Roll dough into circles, place filling, fold into half-moons and seal.
Shallow-fry till golden and crisp on both sides.
Serve hot with tomato-chilli dip or tea.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Tibetan-style fried stuffed bread – popular snack or light meal.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Crisp exterior and juicy filling.

title: Dal Bhat Tarkari
steps: Cook rice and dal separately. Prepare a simple vegetable curry (tarkari) with onion, garlic and spices.
Serve the classic combination of rice, dal, tarkari and achar on a plate.
Add a side of gundruk or kinema for authentic Sikkimese flavour.

fullIngredients.name: Achar (pickle), gundruk or kinema on the side

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The everyday meal pattern of most Sikkimese households (Nepali influence).

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Simple, balanced and nourishing.

title: Chhurpi
steps: Soft chhurpi is made by curdling buttermilk and draining; eaten fresh as a side or in soups.
Hard chhurpi is further dried and becomes a long-lasting chewable cheese.
Serve soft chhurpi with rice or as a snack; hard variety is chewed like gum.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditional Himalayan cheese – soft and hard varieties.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: High-protein, long-shelf-life food suited to mountain life.

title: Ningro (Fiddlehead Fern)
steps: Clean the fiddlehead ferns thoroughly. Blanch if desired.
Heat mustard oil, add garlic and dry red chilli. Stir-fry the ningro with salt till tender-crisp.
Serve as a seasonal side or snack.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Monsoon forest vegetable unique to the eastern Himalayas.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Mild, slightly mucilaginous texture when cooked.

title: Bamboo Shoot Curry
steps: If using fresh bamboo shoot, boil to remove bitterness. Fermented ones can be used directly.
Sauté onion and chilli in mustard oil. Add bamboo shoot, turmeric and salt. Add a little water and simmer.
Serve with rice.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, chilli, turmeric, salt, mustard oil

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Common in Lepcha and other communities – fermented versions add tang.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Pairs well with dal bhat.

title: Dhindo
steps: Bring water to a boil with salt. Gradually add the flour while stirring vigorously with a wooden stick to avoid lumps.
Cook on low heat, stirring continuously, till it forms a thick, soft dough that pulls away from the sides.
Serve scoops with dal, gundruk, achar or any side.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditional dense porridge of millet/buckwheat – filling mountain staple.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Eaten by hand, often with multiple accompaniments.
